column2: Andy Burnham became Prime Minister, succeeding Keir Starmer (who had voted for the assisted dying Bill).
column3: New PM with a social care record as a former Health Secretary; the political frame around assisted dying changed.

column2: PM's social care speech at a north London care home: fixing palliative and social care funding must come first, 'that's the position that I will stick to'. Casey report brought forward to summer 2027; ministerial group; Big Conversation on Care.
column3: This is the promise the campaign holds him to.

column2: PM's letter to the PLP: he will not vote at Second Reading and will implement Parliament's will 'whether that is to change the law or not'. Collective responsibility waived.
column3: Removed the Government from the fight; made the PM's own test the only thing left standing after the vote.

column2: CitizenGO delivered the petition against the Bill (18429: 23,130 signatures, 1,659 new members).
column3: The audience for this follow-up; they were told care was the answer.

column2: Second Reading of the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill rejected 270-286 (div. 2428). Hospice UK asked the PM for 'meaningful action'; Ashley Dalton MP told the House to 'sort out social and palliative care'.
column3: Parliament settled the question the PM said had to wait; his condition became a debt.

column2: Brief drafted. Decisions: headline promise with three dated tests (Budget 28 Oct, Modern Service Framework autumn, Casey summer 2027); assisted suicide front and centre but never a precondition for legalisation; 5CA on the PM and related ministers only; Obligatory campaign; title 'Prime Minister, keep your word: fund hospices now'; hospices lead, social care is Test 3; Hospice UK's GBP 112.5m the starting measure; delivery attempted at Labour conference 29 Sept, by email if refused.
column3: Sets the shape of the campaign and the scorecard the report-backs will use.
